question: ATLAS is the protocol the king and the double sharings are already in MP-SPDZ for. What does it cost, and what does moving from 7 nodes to 9 cost, since n >= 4T+1 is what the decoding route needs?
load_caveat: host-a was at load average 37 of 64 vCPU during these runs. Traffic and round counts do not depend on load; no wall-clock figure is reported here, and none should be taken from these runs.

setting.phase: single-phase --- triples and double sharings generated in the run, which is the comparison GSZ wants because GSZ has no offline phase

what_reading_the_engine_had_already_esta.shamir: Protocols/Shamir.hpp is GRR re-sharing. No degree-2t opening, so nothing for a decoder to correct.
what_reading_the_engine_had_already_esta.atlas: Protocols/Atlas.hpp is Damgard-Nielsen: get_double_sharing() returns {[r]_2t, [r]_t}, the masked product goes to a king that rotates round-robin, and the king re-shares at degree t.
what_reading_the_engine_had_already_esta.randomness: Shamir<T>::get_randoms uses HYPER-INVERTIBLE MATRICES (get_hyper, PREP_DIR/Hyper-t-n-p) with add_from_all + exchange. That is the same machinery the robust double-sharing generation in the GSZ line is built on, and it is already here.

findings.finding: ATLAS is 0.800x semi-honest Shamir, at BOTH node counts
findings.note: MP-SPDZ's README says ATLAS scales better than plain Shamir; the ratio is flat rather than improving over this range

findings.finding: Moving 7 -> 9 costs 1.167x per party and 1.500x global, and the round count does not move
findings.numbers: atlas 4.572 -> 5.333, semi-honest 5.714 -> 6.667, both 7/6 per party; rounds 9 -> 13 and 4 -> 4 at both n
findings.why_it_matters: n >= 4T+1 is what the decoding route needs, and this is its whole traffic bill

findings.finding: The malicious Shamir baseline on this box is 64.236, not the 48.235 the paper quotes
findings.why: the naming patch (locate-inconsistent-shares) is applied to this build, and decode_patch.json measured exactly 64.236 for it. The deployed-with-naming engine is what a robust protocol has to be compared against now.

findings.finding: ATLAS at n=9 costs 12.0x less per party than the deployed engine at n=7
findings.caveat: ATLAS is SEMI-HONEST. This is headroom, not a result. What it says is that the budget for adding robustness on top of ATLAS is large.

the_decomposition_this_supports.model: ATLAS single-phase = randomness generation + 1 element to the king + the king's re-share amortised over the rotation, so online is about 2 per party.
the_decomposition_this_supports.arithmetic: get_randoms costs (n-1)/(n-t) per random per party at degree t and (n-1)/(n-2t) at degree 2t. At n=7,t=2 that is 1.2 + 2.0 = 3.2, plus 2 online = 5.2 against 4.572 measured (12% high). At n=9 it is 1.143 + 1.6 = 2.74, plus 2 = 4.74 against 5.333 measured (11% low).
the_decomposition_this_supports.verdict: the model is right in shape and wrong by about 12% in both directions, so it is worth using for an estimate and not for a claim

estimate_for_the_robust_variant_which_is.construction: drop the king; open the masked product to all n; each party decodes with Berlekamp-Welch and computes [xy]_t = e - [r]_t locally
estimate_for_the_robust_variant_which_is.online_per_party: n - 1 = 8 at n=9, replacing the king's 2
estimate_for_the_robust_variant_which_is.single_phase_total_per_party: about 11.3 at n=9, with a band of 10 to 13 given the model's 12% error
estimate_for_the_robust_variant_which_is.against_what_is_deployed: about 0.18x of the 64.236 that malicious-shamir-party.x with the naming patch spends at n=7 --- roughly 5.7x cheaper, while never stopping
estimate_for_the_robust_variant_which_is.status: AN ESTIMATE. Nothing robust has been run.

tested: that atlas-party.x runs at n=7 and n=9 with T=2
the cost of the base the robust variant would be built on
the price of n >= 4T+1, which is the whole reason for going to 9 nodes
that the round count is independent of n
not_tested: the predicted 8 elements per party for the robust variant --- that variant does not exist
the predicted 1 round per layer against ATLAS's 2
anything about behaviour under a corrupted party, which is the only thing that would distinguish rung 4 from rung 5

two_things_that_had_to_be_fixed_to_run_t.threshold_flag: MPSpdzRun decided whether to pass -T by `"shamir" in binary`, which silently excluded atlas-party.x. ShamirOptions then defaults to (n-1)/2, so the run would have measured 3-of-7 while the caller asked for 2-of-7. Now an explicit family check.
two_things_that_had_to_be_fixed_to_run_t.ssl: Player-Data held certificates for 7 parties. Every 9-party run failed with `Cannot access Player-Data/P8.pem` on the last party and `Timed out waiting for peer` on the rest --- the message that names the cause appears on ONE party's log out of nine. Scripts/setup-ssl.sh 9.
